item.title: Comment on The exhaustion of rents by Dinwar
item.description:
"It is of course amazing that the local authority owning the dump has no interest in recovering the money for itself."

Tell me you don't understand waste management without saying you don't understand waste management....I've done this sort of thing on landfills. You're going to eat into that 600 million pounds FAST.

I'm not familiar with UK waste management, but in the USA, it would be insanely expensive to find the thing, if it's even there. You have to manage each daily cell, which means tracking everything that went into it. And as soon as you dig it up and put it into a rolloff box (and believe me, you need rolloff boxes for this; stockpiles present too many failure states) you've generated waste. Stuff that was grandfathered into the landfill based on old standards suddenly needs to be managed as hazardous--possibly under multiple legal frameworks, which gets REALLY complicated REALLY quickly. For example, if you have PCB-contaminated soil that also has PCE contamination, it now has to be incinerated. That's assuming that it doesn't just light on fire on contact with the air or explode or something.

You have to do all this while managing runoff, off-gassing, and other hazards. Oh, and landfills are built to keep things from changing. Now that you've excavated them, they will start decaying faster, especially if you put incompatible materials together. Real nasty results, potentially.

You ALSO need to find the thing that has the bitcoin on it--again, assuming it's even there. Which is not going to be a simple as just putting it all on a conveyor belt and looking at it. If you fail in this task, you've taken on all that fiscal and legal liability for nothing.

Now, that's not to say that this is necessarily a bad idea. I think landfills should be mined--historic disposal methods mean that a lot of potentially valuable material is in old landfills. But the reality is that you need to make far more profit than you think in order to make the activity viable. The only way I'd do something like this is if the process would be profitable WITHOUT the bitcoin wallet.

Well, to be honest I'd love for them to do it because I'd put my name in to manage their environmental compliance and mitigation side. That's going to be a few tens of millions alone, if not hundreds of millions, and being in charge of that wouldn't look bad on my resume. And I don't imagine it would be completed before I retire--or before my kids retire, for that matter.

item.title: Comment on Dwarkesh’s Question by Old Programmer
item.description:
LLMs are: useful tools for coding and search.
LLMs are: impressive because it looks like a very solid solution to Natural Language problems

LLMs are not: intelligent.

I suspect they are a portion of a system that may be made in the future that will be intelligent. Perhaps the memory and language parts? It seems like attempts are being made to add reasoning. The approaches currently underway may work. There is a lot of money chasing AI right now.

The science fiction fan in me wonders if qubits will play a role at some point.
